# Zetarya

> Zetarya moves very large files directly between two devices — up to 1 Gbps, encrypted end to end, with nothing stored on our servers. Pair two machines with a six-digit code and the bytes go straight from one to the other.

Zetarya runs on its own protocol over UDP rather than on TCP, which is what lets a single transfer hold a gigabit across a long path. Files are sent as hashed chunks, so a transfer resumes to the byte after a dropped connection, a closed lid, or a switch from Wi-Fi to mobile. Content is encrypted with AES-256 inside TLS 1.3; session keys are generated on the two endpoints and never reach us. Most connections are established directly through NAT hole punching, and fall back to an encrypted relay when a network refuses a direct path.

## Product

- [Features](https://zetarya.com/features): pairing, transfer and control capabilities in full
- [Pricing](https://zetarya.com/pricing): free tier at 30 GB/month up to 40 Mbps; paid tiers up to 10 TB at 1 Gbps
- [Changelog](https://zetarya.com/changelog): release notes by version

## Writing

- [How we hold 1 Gbps on a link that keeps moving](https://zetarya.com/blog/one-gbps-long-haul): why we left TCP, and what we cut

- [Resume, to the byte](https://zetarya.com/blog/resume-to-the-byte): the chunk map behind interrupted transfers
- [What an audit log should not contain](https://zetarya.com/blog/audit-log-should-not-contain): accountability without a filename index
